fact: 1918年5月22日，马德里《ABC》报以头条报道了正在流行的流感，这是西班牙媒体对该次大流行的最早显著报道之一；第一波（1918年5—7月）传染快、死亡率低，第二波在1918年秋暴发并明显更致命。

sources.title: Trilla A., Trilla G., Daer C., The 1918 Spanish Flu in Spain, Clinical Infectious Diseases 47(5), 2008
sources.quote: On 22 May 1918, the epidemic was a headline in Madrid's ABC newspaper. The infectious disease most likely reached Spain from France, perhaps as the result of the heavy railroad traffic of Spanish and Portuguese migrant workers to and from France.

sources.title: Ager P., et al., The Redistributive Effects of Pandemics: Evidence of the Spanish Flu, LSE Economic History Working Paper 308
sources.quote: The first news of an increasing death toll due to respiratory diseases appeared in the Spanish press in May 1918, in the wake of the first wave of the pandemic starting in March 1918. ... This wave peaked in October 1918, with mortality rates increasing by 300 per cent with respect to the pre-influenza mortality rates in October According to some existing estimates, deaths caused by respiratory diseases increased by 2.4 per 10,000 in the first wave of May-July 1918 and by 92.6 per 10,000 during the Fall 1918-Winter 1919 wave.

fact: 1918年11月，加泰罗尼亚的自治机构曼科穆尼达德（Mancomunitat）向马德里议会提交了规定加泰罗尼亚全面自治基本框架的草案，引发西班牙民族主义者的激烈反对，该草案在卡斯蒂利亚议员的一致否决下连辩论程序都未进入。

sources.title: Martorell Linares M. A., Wartime and Post-war Societies (Spain), 1914-1918-online. International Encyclopedia of the First World War
sources.quote: In November 1918, the Mancomunidad presented a draft proposal setting down the basic outlines for full Catalan autonomy to the Madrid Cortes, which unleashed an aggressive Spanish-nationalist campaign of opposition and was not even put to debate, in the face of its flat rejection by the Castilian deputies.

fact: 1918年至1920年，安达卢西亚爆发以无政府主义骨干为主导的大规模农业工人运动，史称「布尔什维克三年」（trienio bolchevique）；同一时期巴斯克钢铁工业和阿斯图里亚斯矿区也出现高强度劳资冲突。

sources.title: Martorell Linares M. A., Wartime and Post-war Societies (Spain), 1914-1918-online
sources.quote: The intense agrarian mobilization in Andalusia between 1918 and 1920, spearheaded principally by anarchist militants, was given the name trienio bolchevique, the “Bolshevik three years”. Levels of conflict were also intense in the Basque iron and steel industry and the mining districts of Asturias

sources.title: Sánchez Picón A., García Gómez J. J., Wartime and Post-war Economies (Spain), 1914-1918-online（表4，据 Carreras & Tafunell 编《Estadísticas Históricas de España》）

fact: 同一部权威百科的另一篇文章给出另一套口径：1913至1918年西班牙物价指数由100升至218，而工资指数仅由100升至125，因此体力工人与依赖薪俸的中产阶层整体丧失购买力；食品与原料价格翻倍。该口径与本包 1918-ES-COST-001 的消费物价指数（1918年为156.08）并不一致。

sources.title: Martorell Linares M. A., Wartime and Post-war Societies (Spain), 1914-1918-online
sources.quote: The result was a shortage in supplies of foodstuffs and raw materials, the prices of which, moreover, doubled. Although employment and wages increased in the sectors favoured by the new circumstances, overall the index of prices rose between 1913 and 1918 from a base of 100 to 218, while the index of wages rose only from 100 to 125, so that as a whole manual workers and the middle classes dependent on salaries lost purchasing power.

sources.title: Sánchez Picón A., García Gómez J. J., Wartime and Post-war Economies (Spain), 1914-1918-online
sources.quote: While inflation in the country as a whole was notably lower than that of the European countries at war ... Prices almost doubled between 1914 and 1920 and then remained stable until the Spanish Civil War.

fact: 西班牙在第一次世界大战期间保持中立，未实行交战国式的战时新闻审查，报纸可以自由报道疫情与战况；正因如此，1918年西班牙的疫情消息最早被英语媒体广泛转载，这也成为「西班牙流感」这一误称的直接来源。

sources.title: Phillips H., Influenza Pandemic, 1914-1918-online. International Encyclopedia of the First World War
sources.quote: Though this first wave of the pandemic laid millions low, it claimed relatively few lives and was most noted for the disruption of everyday activities which it caused among troops and civilians alike and for the fact that such disruptions in neutral Spain (where no censorship of the press was in force) were widely reported in the world's media, earning it the mistaken tag of "Spanish" flu.

fact: 自1914年8月3日起，西班牙禁止出口煤、黄金、白银、牲畜、谷物、蔬菜、肉类与家禽、大米和马铃薯，另有一项法令降低小麦进口税以期压低粮价；但这些以及后续同类指令「全都没有效果」，国内短缺与涨价持续到1918年。

sources.title: Martorell Linares M. A., Wartime and Post-war Societies (Spain), 1914-1918-online
sources.quote: from 3 August 1914 the export of coal, gold, silver, livestock, cereals, vegetables, meat and poultry, rice and potatoes were all prohibited, and another ruling reduced import duties on wheat in the hope of reducing grain prices. However, these and subsequent similar directives were all ineffective.

fact: 西班牙银行（Banco de España）的黄金储备由1914年的7.11亿金比塞塔增至1918年的25亿金比塞塔；顺差的三条主要去向是增加黄金储备、购回外债与外资持有的西班牙股票债券（1914年约14亿比塞塔）、以及换取比塞塔或外币存款。

sources.title: Sánchez Picón A., García Gómez J. J., Wartime and Post-war Economies (Spain), 1914-1918-online（引 Sudrià）
sources.quote: According to Sudrià, the surpluses in the balance of payments had three main destinations: to increase the gold reserves of the Bank of Spain (from 711 million gold pesetas in 1914 to 2.5 billion gold pesetas in 1918), to purchase Spanish financial assets, both outstanding external debt and shares and debt securities which were foreign-owned in 1914 (around 1.4 billion pesetas), and to obtain deposits in pesetas or foreign currency.

fact: 战争期间积累的外币在战后贬值，持有者因此陷入债务；战争利润也没有转为再投资，固定资本形成占GDP的比重反而下降，因为工业家难以买到外国机器。结果是银行成为主要受益者——资金以存款形式留在银行，成为1920年代大型实业项目的融资来源。

sources.title: Sánchez Picón A., García Gómez J. J., Wartime and Post-war Economies (Spain), 1914-1918-online
sources.quote: In the latter case, the currencies were used for speculation or remained inactive. When the war was over, these currencies depreciated and lost their value, plunging their holders into debt. Profits earned from the war were not used for reinvestment, so gross fixed capital formation's share of GDP fell. ... This meant that the banks were the main beneficiaries, as this capital remained in the form of deposits, enabling them to finance large business projects in the 1920s.

fact: 钨价从1914年的每吨16,600美元涨至1916年的70,600美元，1919年又跌回23,600美元；西班牙钨矿开采在1916、1917、1918年特别扩张，其中许多活动并不合法（走私与越界开采），战后该金属几乎被遗忘，直到第二次世界大战才再度受重视。

sources.title: Caruana de las Cagigas L., González Calleja E., La producción y el contrabando de wolframio en España durante la Primera Guerra Mundial, Ayer 95 (2014), 摘要
sources.quote: La extracción minera se incrementó especialmente en los años 1916, 1917 y 1918, con actividades, muchas de ellas, nada lícitas. Al concluir la contienda, este metal volvió a ser casi olvidado hasta la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

fact: 按 Carreras 编制的工业产值指数（1913=100），西班牙1914年为99.68，1916年109.02，1917年106.96，1918年108.86，1919年100.95；1914—1919年年均增长仅0.25%，1919年产出相对1913年仅增约1%。战争带来的是利润与出口结构变化，而非工业产能的实质扩张。

sources.title: Sánchez Picón A., García Gómez J. J., Wartime and Post-war Economies (Spain), 1914-1918-online（表5）
sources.quote: Industrial production index 1913=100 1913 100.00 1914 99.68 1915 104.11 1916 109.02 1917 106.96 1918 108.86 1919 100.95 ... The industrial production index calculated by Albert Carreras shows an inter-annual growth of 0.25 percent between 1914 and 1919; Spanish industry only increased its output by 1 percent from 1913.

fact: 1918年西班牙流感死亡人数存在三个互不一致的口径：官方估计1918年死于流感者147,114人（1919年21,235人、1920年17,825人）；Trilla 等认为实际可能超过26万人；Johnson 与 Mueller 的跨国统计表列为257,082人、死亡率12.3‰。本包并列三说，不取单一数字为定论。

sources.title: Trilla A., Trilla G., Daer C., The 1918 Spanish Flu in Spain, Clinical Infectious Diseases 47(5), 2008
sources.quote: The total numbers of persons who died of influenza in Spain were officially estimated to be 147,114 in 1918, 21,235 in 1919, and 17,825 in 1920. However, it is likely that >260,000 Spaniards died of influenza

sources.title: Ager P., et al., The Redistributive Effects of Pandemics: Evidence of the Spanish Flu, LSE Economic History Working Paper 308（表1，据 Johnson & Mueller 2002）
sources.quote: Spain 257,082 12.3 ... Table 1: Mortality rates per 1,000, Spanish Flu. Sources: Johnson and Mueller (2002)

fact: 西班牙的流感死亡高度集中于第二波：约75%的死者死于第二波，其中45%集中在1918年10月一个月内；1918年西班牙人口增长指数为负，净减少83,121人。死亡率在25—34岁年龄组最高，65岁以上反而低于常态。

sources.title: Trilla A., Trilla G., Daer C., The 1918 Spanish Flu in Spain, Clinical Infectious Diseases 47(5), 2008
sources.quote: 75% of these persons died during the second period of the epidemic, and 45% died during October 1918 alone. The Spanish population growth index was negative for 1918 (net loss, 83,121 persons).

sources.title: Ager P., et al., The Redistributive Effects of Pandemics: Evidence of the Spanish Flu, LSE Working Paper 308
sources.quote: Mortality rates were higher in the 25-34 age group, while there were below trend among those above 65. As a result of the pandemic, Spain's population growth was negative in 1918 (net loss of 83,121 persons).

fact: 1918年秋西班牙采取的公共卫生措施包括：学校与大学停课、用次氯酸钠水冲洗街道、对火车、电车、行李、酒吧、咖啡馆乃至邮件用酚油定期消毒；但弥撒与其他大型集会照常举行，社交距离与消毒建议「难以强制执行」。

sources.title: Ager P., et al., The Redistributive Effects of Pandemics: Evidence of the Spanish Flu, LSE Economic History Working Paper 308
sources.quote: Schools and universities were closed, but mass and other gatherings were still organized, facilitating the spread of the virus. Some public health measures were adopted: streets were cleaned with water and sodium hypochlorite. Trains, tramways, baggages, bars, cafeterias, even the mail, were regularly disinfected with phenolic oil. Social distancing and disinfection measures were recommended by state authorities, but these measures were difficult to enforce.

fact: 「西班牙流感」是误称而非起源地标记：1918年6月2日伦敦《泰晤士报》马德里通讯员已称其为「西班牙流行病」，三周后该报又称「今天人人都把它当作西班牙流感」；西班牙人自己则按当时马德里上演的轻歌剧歌曲称之为「那不勒斯士兵」，或主张它来自法国战场。现有研究普遍认为1918年H1N1病毒不太可能起源并传播自西班牙。

sources.title: Phillips H., Influenza Pandemic, 1914-1918-online
sources.quote: Already on 2 June 1918, the Times' Madrid correspondent referred to it as 'The Spanish Epidemic,' ... while three weeks later that newspaper breezily reported that 'Everybody thinks of it as the Spanish influenza today' ... In turn, indignant Spaniards called it 'The Naples Soldier,' after a catchy song in an operetta by that name then being performed in Madrid, or they claimed that it came from the battlefields of France.

sources.title: Trilla A., Trilla G., Daer C., The 1918 Spanish Flu in Spain, Clinical Infectious Diseases 47(5), 2008
sources.quote: Although a great deal of evidence indicates that the 1918 A(H1N1) influenza virus unlikely originated in and spread from Spain, the 1918-1919 influenza pandemic will always be known as the Spanish flu.

fact: 西班牙年罢工数由1913年的约200起增至1919年的400起以上；1916年12月18日社会党UGT与无政府工团CNT联合发动的一日总罢工「取得显著成功」，停工蔓延到所有主要城市，并获得小店主、白领与中产的同情。

sources.title: Martorell Linares M. A., Wartime and Post-war Societies (Spain), 1914-1918-online
sources.quote: The annual number of strikes doubled: if in 1913 there were around 200 strikes during the year, in 1919 there were more than 400. ... Held on 18 December, it was a notable success. Stoppages of work extended to all the major cities
